tasks.title: T/W at the requirement's conditions
tasks.statement: On the stand, one motor with its prop gave **{thr} g** at **{v0} V** under load and +20 °C. Requirement: T/W ≥ 2.5 at **{v} V** and air at **+{t} °C**. Takeoff mass **{m} g**, four motors, thrust at full throttle ∝ V^1.8, air density ∝ 1/T_abs at the same pressure. Find T/W at the requirement's conditions.
tasks.solution: T/W = 4·T·(V/V₀)^1.8·(293.15/(273.15 + t))/m. Both corrections are less than one: the end of the flight and the heat reduce thrust, so the bench T/W without corrections is overestimated. The module's example: 4·750·0.7863·0.9513/860 = 2.610.

tasks.title: Expanded uncertainty of T/W
tasks.statement: T/W budget: stand calibration **U = {c} %** (k = 2, one for all four motors); unit-to-unit spread of motor + prop **{s} %** per unit relative to the batch mean (k = 1). **One of the four installed** motors was measured on the stand, and its thrust was multiplied by four. Scales **±{a} g** (uniform distribution) at a mass of **{m} g**. Find the relative expanded uncertainty of T/W at k = 2, %.
tasks.solution: Calibration: u = U/2, not divided over the sum of the four motors (a common source). Spread: the sum of four differs from 4·T₁ by e₂ + e₃ + e₄ − 3e₁, hence u = s·√12/4 ≈ 0.866·s (not s/√4: the deviation of the measured motor enters all four). Scales: a/√3/m·100 %. U = 2·√((c/2)² + (s·√12/4)² + (a/√3/m·100)²). The module's example (0.61 %, 3 %, ±2 g, 860 g, no corrections): 2·√(0.305² + 2.598² + 0.134²) = 5.24 %; if T₁ were the batch mean over many measurements, s/2 would stand in place of s·√12/4.

tasks.title: Decision with a guard band
tasks.statement: Measured T/W = **{y}**, combined relative standard uncertainty **u_c = {u} %**. Requirement T/W ≥ 2.5. Find the lower bound T/W − U at k = 2 (the decision is made by it: ≥ 2.5 — met, otherwise — not proven or not met).
tasks.solution: U = 2·u_c·y, lower bound = y·(1 − 2·u_c). The module's example (u_c = 3.38 %): 2.610·(1 − 0.0676) = 2.434 < 2.5 → “not proven”, even though the mean is 4 % above the limit. If the upper bound y·(1 + 2·u_c) is also below 2.5 — “not met”.
